newsitem.title: USA: Florida mulls divestiture of tobacco stocks.
newsitem.headline: Florida mulls divestiture of tobacco stocks.

text.p: Florida Board of Administration is studying whether the state should divest $693 million of tobacco stocks held by the state pension fund, St. Petersburg Times reported Tuesday.
The stocks represent about 1.3 percent of the $53.3 billion pension fund that covers 600,000 current state, county, city and school employees and 153,000 retirees.
Comptroller Bob Milligan, who quit smoking 10 years ago, said he supports efforts to reduce smoking but that safeguarding the fund should be the chief consideration.
"My responsibility is not a social one. It is a responsibility to the present and future retirees of the state of Florida that we make the best use of those retirement funds," Milligan said.

Milligan, Gov Lawton Chiles and Insurance Commissioner Bill Nelson make up the state Board of Administration, which oversees the pension fund. All were in a state Cabinet meeting Tuesday and could not be reached for comment.

Chiles, a former smoker who chews tobacco, said he would prefer that the state divest its tobacco stocks but would await a thorough review by the administration board's staff and legal advisors. The review is expected by the end of the year.
Chiles is among the governors who have sued the tobacco industry to recover public funds spent treating smoking-related illnesses.
